{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Cyclone was a wooden roller coaster that operated at Revere Beach in Revere, Massachusetts, from 1925 until 1969.","title":"Cyclone (Revere Beach)"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" When Cyclone was constructed, it was the tallest roller coaster ever built, as well as being the first roller coaster in the world to reach 100 ft in height.","title":"Cyclone (Revere Beach)"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" In addition to being the tallest roller coaster of its day, some also claim that it was the largest and fastest roller coaster in the world, with a length of 3600 ft and top speeds between 45 and 50 mph (some dispute the speed record claim and instead award that honor to the Giant Dipper).","title":"Cyclone (Revere Beach)"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Cyclone held the title of world's tallest roller coaster until 1964 when it was surpassed by Montaña Rusa at La Feria Chapultepec Mágico in Mexico City, Mexico.","title":"Cyclone (Revere Beach)"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Magnum XL-200, colloquially known as simply Magnum, is a steel roller coaster built by Arrow Dynamics at Cedar Point in Sandusky, Ohio.","title":"Magnum XL-200"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" When built in 1989, it was the tallest, fastest, and steepest complete-circuit roller coaster in the world as well as the first hypercoaster – a roller coaster that exceeds 200 ft in height.","title":"Magnum XL-200"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Some have credited Magnum with starting a period in the industry known as the \"roller coaster wars\", in which amusement parks competed with one another at a rapid pace to build the next tallest and fastest roller coaster.","title":"Magnum XL-200"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" More than 40 million people had ridden Magnum as of 2009.","title":"Magnum XL-200"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"Skyplex has which roller coaster that will become the tallest in the world when it opens in 2020?"}
